title: The URL
logline: Tuesday. The name can't be changed: the address is the address now, forty thousand people have it. Wood, small, at the CRT, typing ROFLCOPTER and watching it not be the thing anyone comes to.

panels.composition: The garage. WOOD, two-thirds, at the CRT — the keyboard too big, his hands spread. BARNABY, normal, larger than him lying down.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a small man at a CRT monitor with a keyboard too big for his hands in a dark garage, a normal-sized dog lying beside him larger than he is

panels.composition: The address bar. He types the name right: R-O-F-L-C-O-P-T-E-R. Enter. A blank page: NOT FOUND.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, close-up of a browser address bar with a correctly spelled name typed and the page below reading NOT FOUND
image.notes: Letter after: the correct spelling, then NOT FOUND. The misspelling is the address; the strip's future name is a dead link in 2006.

panels.composition: He types it wrong: R-O-L-F-C-O-P-T-R. Enter. The stick figure. Forty thousand.
props: the address bar, the misspelling, the figure

image.prompt: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, close-up of a browser address bar with a misspelled name typed and a crude stick figure with a rotor appearing on the page below

panels.composition: Wood, small, looking at the screen. The dog's chin on his knee, the chin as big as the knee.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with saturated neon monitor glow cutting through a dark garage, jagged hyperactive linework, muddy digital flats, a small man looking at a monitor with a normal-sized dog's chin resting on his knee, the chin nearly as large as the knee
